scope: Non-normative, paraphrased source observations for editor and scanner review; these notes do not amend frozen 0.4 semantics.

fields.key: Registry subkey within the user's HKCU-equivalent hive; omit the hive prefix when selecting a key.
fields.name: Registry value name. The legacy object distinguishes an empty name (default value) from a nil name (test the key itself); verify native nullable-selector behavior independently.
fields.sid: Windows security identifier associated with the user profile.
fields.username: User name, commonly qualified by computer or domain. Legacy OVAL recommends case-insensitive comparisons for Windows account names.
fields.account_type: Distinguishes local and domain user profiles.
fields.logged_on: Legacy guidance offers loaded HKEY_USERS profile SID comparison as an indicator, while allowing other Windows APIs to corroborate logon sessions.
fields.days_since_last_logon: Legacy guidance derives a day count from ProfileList load-time values, rounding downward; it specifies zero for an account considered currently logged on.
fields.user_has_signed_into_explorer: Legacy source points to a per-profile Explorer UserSigned indicator to distinguish interactive Explorer usage from some noninteractive sessions.
fields.enabled: Account enabled status may be unavailable for domain users without a domain controller. Legacy guidance distinguishes unavailable evidence from a disabled account.
fields.date_modified: Legacy field describes a 64-bit Windows FILETIME for the profile file, measured in 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01 UTC.
fields.days_since_modified: Legacy guidance counts days since the profile hive file changed and rounds upward.
fields.filepath: Path to the corresponding user's ntuser.dat profile hive.
fields.last_write_time: Registry hive/key/value write timestamp in Windows FILETIME units; precise scope depends on the collected registry location.
fields.type: Registry data type of the selected value. Source OVAL enums and native value mapping must be cross-checked; a special legacy empty state is not a collected type.
fields.value: Actual registry data. Legacy guidance distinguishes hex-encoded binary, numeric DWORD/QWORD, unexpanded expandable strings, and multiple entries for multi-string values. Native datatype and cardinality need independent validation.

scanner_observations.summary: The legacy scanner profile-discovery recipe starts from the Windows ProfileList registry key and ProfileImagePath, with SID-pattern screening for human profiles. Verify profile and service-account exclusions before adopting.
Loaded profiles can be observed under HKEY_USERS by SID; unloaded profiles may require reading their NTUSER.DAT files. These access paths need equivalent item identity and error handling.
Avoid operations that lock an original unloaded NTUSER.DAT and interfere with later interactive logon. Choose a safe read strategy and test concurrent profile activity.

The legacy object distinguishes a default registry value from a key-only request and forbids recursion with non-equality key selection; native nullable selectors and traversal constraints must be verified.
Missing domain-controller access can make account-enabled state unavailable; scanner results should distinguish missing acquisition from a real false value.
Legacy Windows FILETIME, profile age rounding, registry type conversions and multi-string value cardinality require explicit native tests before implementation qualification.
